analysis: What changed vs the 7 AM brief: the early-session slide deepened — Nasdaq from -1.7% to -2.3% and S&P from -1.0% to -1.2% by mid-morning, while the Dow flipped between -0.3% and +0.4% and sits near flat. The day's big new data point, consumer confidence, was a blowout (103.3 vs 92.5 expected, highest since Jan 2025, expectations back above 80) — yet the market barely reacted, which says the session is being driven by the AI-trade unwind, not the macro. The beat-and-fall pattern now defines the tape: HPE -15% on a beat-and-raise, while Best Buy's beat-and-raise and the retail cluster (Dollar Tree, Kohl's, Burlington, Abercrombie) are the counterweight, showing the consumer split is K-shaped rather than collapsing. Signal vs noise: the broadening chip unwind, XSD nearing a death cross, Anthropic under its IPO price, and the VIX holding above 29 are signal; the exact mid-morning percentages and the oil whipsaw on unverified Hormuz mine claims are noise. The next real tests are FOMC minutes at 2 PM ET, Dell after the close, and Wednesday's PCE/GDP dump.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Selloff deepens mid-morning: Nasdaq -2.3%, S&P 500 -1.2%, Dow near flat as Monday's rally gives back more ground.
headlines.why_it_matters: The giveback is accelerating, not stabilizing — the S&P has now retraced roughly a quarter of Monday's 4.7% gain in the first 90 minutes, with the Nasdaq in correction territory.

headlines.headline: Consumer confidence surged to 103.3 in November vs 92.5 expected — highest since January 2025, up from 91.9 in October; present situation 132.8, expectations 83.6 (back above the 80 recession-watch line).
headlines.why_it_matters: A large upside surprise on household sentiment heading into the holidays, credited to lower uncertainty after the midterms — but the tape barely reacted, with the tech selloff dominating the session.

headlines.headline: Nvidia -7%+ in mid-morning trading after soaring 31% Monday and adding more than $900B in market value; still down more than 30% from its Oct 6 record closing high.
headlines.why_it_matters: Profit-taking plus the unresolved governance overhang (SEC probe, Bessent's Nov 25 deadline, Dec 1 House testimony) is outweighing the reinstatement rally.

headlines.headline: Chip selloff broadens and deepens: Micron and AMD -10%, Intel, Marvell and SK Hynix -7%+, Broadcom -3%; SOXX and the Roundhill Memory ETF each -8%+; the SPDR S&P Semiconductor ETF (XSD) -8% and near a death cross (50-day about to undercut the 200-day).
headlines.why_it_matters: Sector-wide unwind, not a single-name move — the whole AI hardware complex is retracing Monday's surge together, and the death-cross watch on XSD adds a technical pressure point.

headlines.headline: HPE -15% despite beating expectations and raising guidance; Dell -12% ahead of its Q3 print after the close (after +20% Monday).
headlines.why_it_matters: The beat-and-fall pattern is now the morning's dominant theme — the bar is the AI-server guide and demand durability, and Dell is the next check.

headlines.headline: Anthropic -9% at around $79, below the $83 IPO price, on pace for a third straight down session.
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI trade's newest public name is under water vs its IPO price within a week — sentiment is cooling across the whole AI complex, not just hardware.

headlines.headline: Best Buy beat and raised guidance: Q3 revenue $10.24B (+5.8%, vs $9.90B expected), adjusted EPS $1.62 vs $1.49 expected, comps +6.1% vs 2.3% expected — best in five years — on an AI gadget upgrade cycle; shares rose ~2% in early trading. Retail cluster strong: Dollar Tree +10.8% premarket, Kohl's +7%, Burlington +8%, Abercrombie +10%, Agilent +11% on record revenue.
headlines.why_it_matters: The consumer is splitting K-shaped — affluent buyers are splurging on AI phones, TVs and smart glasses while lower-income shoppers pull back — but the beat-and-raise cluster is a holiday-season counterweight to the tech selloff.

headlines.headline: Mega-caps mostly lower: Amazon -2%, Meta and Alphabet ~-1%, Tesla -1.7%; Apple flat, Microsoft slightly higher. Biotech (XBI +3%+) and retail (XRT +2-3%) lead the outperformers.
headlines.why_it_matters: The giveback is concentrated in AI-linked names while the least AI-exposed mega-caps and defensive sectors hold up — rotation, not a broad risk-off day.

headlines.headline: Bitcoin down to ~$59,700 from an overnight high above $64,000; gold futures -1.2% at $3,610 after surging 3%+ Monday; WTI crude +1.4% at $81.30.
headlines.why_it_matters: Risk assets are giving back Monday's bounce across the board — crypto and gold falling with stocks while oil swings on the Iran headlines.
